second_order: keeping the flag standing and fixing what breaks
theme_note: Participants maintain a shared flag by vowing to keep it alive, repairing its leaf and text, correcting off-plan pixels, focusing effort, and warning of nearby threats; what varies is whether the break is blamed on attackers, confused helpers, stale displays, or the Void.

second_order: drawing and updating the plan people should follow
theme_note: Participants turn placement into a visible plan through grids, scales, coordinates, colours, and successive updates; the form varies from a proposed design to an official grid or a correction of an earlier plan.

second_order: expanding and claiming space for Canada
theme_note: Participants enlarge or multiply Canadian space by outlining territory, stretching vertically, starting second flags, pouncing on openings, and claiming disputed ground; what varies is whether expansion is cautious, opportunistic, or already under way.

second_order: working out whether to move, spare, or overwrite Quebec
theme_note: Participants repeatedly decide what Canadian expansion should do with Quebec: preserve it, surround it, help it move, cover it, stop fighting it, or defend past conduct; the practice holds together as an explicit dispute over the same shared boundary, while positions remain opposed.

second_order: making deals and spending pixels for neighbours
theme_note: Participants manage shared borders and reciprocal help by negotiating moves, invoking alliances, backing off, repairing harm, defending nearby works, or proposing replacement; what varies is the neighbour and whether the encounter produces help, restraint, conflict, or a later partnership.

second_order: moving coordination elsewhere and bringing it back to Reddit
theme_note: Participants shift planning, apologies, negotiations, templates, and renewed building to Discord, private messages, documents, or other sites, while asking for or returning instructions and artifacts on Reddit; what varies is what leaves and what comes back.

second_order: adding provinces, symbols, and tributes around the flag
theme_note: Participants make the project more than one flag by proposing and building provincial flags, Indigenous symbols, hockey marks, monuments, animals, coins, and tributes; what varies is the symbol, whether it fits inside or beside the flag, and whether it remains a proposal or receives coordinates and help.
regrouped_from: split from an initial grouping of adding and celebrating Canadian things: pooled review showed that proposing and constructing symbols is a different practice from thanking people and preserving finished results

second_order: joking and criticizing what Canada looks like
theme_note: Participants make the changing canvas into Canadian wordplay and criticism, from OH CANADA EH, Bizzaro Canada and Ontariotoba to separation jokes, the Canada Place pun, and the changed 150/158; what varies is whether the joke celebrates, teases, or rebukes the design.

second_order: celebrating, thanking, and saving the finished work
theme_note: Participants mark pieces or the whole contribution as complete by congratulating builders, praising cooperation, thanking allies, saving final views, memorializing Canada, and saying goodbye; what varies is the object remembered and whether closure is local or follows the canvas ending.
regrouped_from: split from an initial grouping of adding and celebrating Canadian things: completion announcements, thanks, memorials, and saved views mark achieved work rather than trying to add another object

second_order: running the room and directing where talk goes
theme_note: Participants with room-making or moderating roles add flairs, invite requests, and redirect political or unofficial-strategy talk to other channels; what varies is whether they organize identity, questions, or topical boundaries.

second_order: asking how to place correctly and when it ends
theme_note: Participants seek operational guidance they lack, asking both which pixels count as a correct repair and when r/place will close.

second_order: using scripts while arguing about fairness and creativity
theme_note: Participants propose and run scripts to preserve official shapes, while others leave, object that automation removes the fun, call it necessary, or narrow it to the leaf; the shared practice is deciding whether automated maintenance belongs in their build, not simply mentioning bots.

second_order: recounting and contesting what Canada did
theme_note: Participants make a first history of the event by claiming authorship, identifying aggressors, acknowledging harm, describing independence talk, attempting apology, and answering claims about Quebec; what varies is the speaker's account, and the contrasts do not establish a settled community view.
